Green Party nominee Risa Lombardo and No Labels nominee Teri Ann Hourihan won their parties' primaries and are also on the November ballot. candidates.name: Katie Hobbs
candidates.background: Governor of Arizona since 2023; former Secretary of State and social worker.

housing.label: Vetoed 2024 bill cutting construction regulations as 'a step too far' (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Mixed: deployed the National Guard to the border; proposed scholarships for undocumented students (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Mixed: created independent prison oversight; resumed executions after a pause (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Signed repeal of Arizona's 1864 abortion ban; backs viability protections (Prop 139) (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: As SoS, defended 2020 results and criticized the Maricopa 'audit' as conspiracy-chasing (Wikipedia)

cost.label: Proposed a state child tax credit and sales-tax exemptions for diapers, formula and OTC medicines (Ballotpedia)

health.label: 'Worked across the aisle to expand Medicaid'; proposed 12-month postpartum Medicaid coverage (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Voted against 'the Republicans' massive corporate tax cuts' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Budget caps ESA vouchers by income, calls the program an entitlement; $285.6M more K-12 funding (Arizona Mirror)

climate.label: Joined the U.S. Climate Alliance, committing Arizona to Paris-aligned emissions cuts of 50 to 52 percent by 2030 and net-zero by 2050 (U.S. Climate Alliance)

candidates.now: Governor of Arizona

candidates.now: Green Party nominee for Arizona governor
candidates.background: Lombardo is the Green Party nominee for Arizona governor. She was a registered Democrat from 2006 to 2016, then voted in Republican primaries and served as an elected Republican precinct committeeman before switching to Green Party registration in 2025. candidates.name: Teri Ann Hourihan

sources.label: KJZZ: Underdog candidate bests well-funded opponent in Arizona's first No Labels gubernatorial primary
Arizona Capitol Times: No Labels' Hourihan names running mate

candidates.now: No Labels Party nominee for Arizona governor; mental health counselor
candidates.background: Hourihan is a Phoenix-based Licensed Professional Counselor with a Ph.D. who won Arizona's first No Labels Party gubernatorial primary in July 2026 despite being outspent by her opponent. She has described trying both Democratic and Republican registration before settling into an independent, No Labels approach, saying party politics felt like being pigeonholed. Her campaign rejects PAC, corporate, and AIPAC funding, and she named a running mate in August 2026 ahead of the general election.
priorities: Keeping the school voucher program while improving public schools

cost.label: Campaign site proposes 'stronger oversight of fuel pricing' and rebate programs for teachers, first responders and public servants to ease financial burdens (Teri Ann Hourihan campaign)

health.label: Campaign site calls for 'employer rebate and incentive programs' and more price transparency to make care affordable while supporting independent providers (Teri Ann Hourihan campaign)

housing.label: Campaign site proposes 'adaptive reuse of vacant buildings' for affordable housing (Teri Ann Hourihan campaign)

education.label: Said she differs from Gov. Hobbs by supporting 'keeping Arizona's expanded school voucher program in place while also looking for ways to improve the state's public school system' (KJZZ)

taxes.label: Tax page says 'Tax increases should be a last resort, not a solution to poor financial management' and calls for reducing the tax burden on Arizona families, homeowners, retirees, and small businesses (teriann4azgov.org).

repro.label: Abortion page pledges to preserve Arizona's current abortion laws, saying she 'will not seek to overturn the abortion laws that Arizonans have approved at the ballot box' (teriann4azgov.org).

safety.label: Courts and prisons page says minors 'should be held accountable' and backs prosecuting some as adults, while also stating 'accountability and rehabilitation can work together' through expanded job training, substance abuse treatment, mental health services, and reentry programs (teriann4azgov.org).
